rv.q: Played straight through at 90 minutes and resolutely focused on local politics, it becomes universal by being so specific. … Each of these characters is a victim of the system, hanging on, just … Maxwell Martin is subtly brilliant

Manuel HarlanDirector Matthew Warchus has rearranged the Old Vic so that the audience sits on either side of a narrow strip of stage, but he struggles to generate much in the way of tension, the pace further hampered by long scene changes in which desks are shifted around.
Penhall’s dialogue is packed with zap and zing … the performances are pretty much faultless … the play is at once too narrow and too broad
The dialogue is heavy with explanation and the action slowed by overload … what a versatile actor he is. … an actor of range and substance … Maxwell Martin is terrific
Penhall’s script is not a polemic and brings out the humanity in the characters … The pair have excellent chemistry and their shifting relationship is very believable.
The ideas occasionally supersede the people, but the strong cast, and a good amount of humour in Penhall's script, keep us gripped.

Corden isn’t a subtle actor, painting with broad, blunt colours, and possessed of a monotonous line delivery that flattens much of his dialogue, but his unique combination of manic energy, bluster and simmering aggression work well for the character.
